VASP offers two different GPU ports. An OpenACC port targeting NVIDIA GPUs, and an OpenMP offloading port for AMD and Intel GPUs.

<u>''NVIDIA''</u>

With VASP.6.2.0 we officially released the OpenACC GPU-port of VASP for NVIDIA GPUs:
Official in the sense that we now strongly recommend using this OpenACC version to run VASP on NVIDIA GPU-accelerated systems.

The previous [[CUDA-C GPU port of VASP|CUDA-C GPU-port of VASP]] is considered to be deprecated and is no longer actively developed, maintained, or supported.
As of VASP.6.3.0, the CUDA-C GPU-port of VASP has been dropped completely.

<u>''AMD and Intel''</u>

With VASP.6.6.0 we released an experimental OpenMP GPU-port of VASP, targeting AMD and Intel datacenter GPUs.
Experimental in the sense that we have not fully documented the port. We have thoroughly tested the port on several HPC clusters, but without some adoption by the user base and the port being tested in real scientific workloads, we expect some bugs to remain in edge case problems.
The OpenMP offload GPU-port is based on the well-tested and widely adopted port for NVIDIA GPUs, but a substantial amount of code has been optimized for the specific vendors.

== Requirements ==

=== Software stacks ===

==== NVIDIA GPUs ====

<u>''Compiler''</u>
* To compile the OpenACC version of VASP you need a recent version of the [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC-SDK] (>=21.2).
:In principle, any compiler that supports at least OpenACC standard 2.6 should do the trick, but we have only tried and tested the aforementioned ones.
{{NB|warning|the NVIDIA HPC-SDK versions 22.1 and 22.2 have a serious bug that prohibits the execution of the OpenACC version in conjunction with OpenMP-threading. When using these compiler versions you should compile without OpenMP support. This bug is fixed as of NVIDIA HPC-SDK version 22.3.|:}}

<u>''Libraries''</u>
* Numerical libraries: FFTW, BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK. In case you are using the [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC-SDK] the only numerical library you will have to install yourself is [http://www.fftw.org FFTW]. The latter three (BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK) are shipped with the SDK. Alternatively, you can link against an installation of [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/onemkl.html Intel's oneAPI MKL] library that provides all four.
* [https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-toolkit The NVIDIA CUDA Toolkit] (>=10.0). All necessary CUDA Toolkit components are shipped as part of the NVIDIA HPC-SDK.
* A CUDA-aware version of MPI. The OpenMPI installations that are packaged with the NVIDIA HPC-SDK are CUDA-aware. MPICH will also work on Cray machines, but the precompiler flag [[Precompiler_options#-DCRAY_MPICH|-DCRAY_MPICH]] has to be added to the [[Makefile.include#NVIDIA_HPC-SDK_for_CPU_and_GPU|makefile.include]].
* [https://developer.nvidia.com/nccl The NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL)] (>=2.7.8). This library is not a strict requirement but its use is highly recommended for performance reasons. Suitable installations of NCCL are shipped as part of the NVIDIA HPC-SDK.

<u>''Drivers''</u>
* You need a CUDA driver that supports at least CUDA-10.0. Note that you have to adapt the [[makefile.include]] for your specific CUDA version. You can query it, e.g., by <code>nvcc --version</code>.
* You will also need to specify for which GPU architectures you want to generate device code for in the [[makefile.include]]. Consult the [https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda/gpus| CUDA GPU Compute Capability] chart to select the compute capabilities (cc), e.g., <code>cc80,cc89</code> for compute capability 8.0 (A series datacenter GPUs) and 8.9 (RTX Ada series workstation GPUs). Selecting more compute capabilities will make your executable more portable, but will increase compile time. If you are compiling on a compute node directly, you can also use <code>ccnative</code>.

==== AMD GPUs ====

<u>''Compiler''</u>
* To compile the OpenMP offload version of VASP for AMD GPUs, the [https://cpe.ext.hpe.com/docs/25.03/cce/index.html HPE Cray compiler environment] (CCE >= 19.0) is needed. This compiler is only available on HPE HPC clusters and cannot be obtained as a stand-alone product. <ref>We are working alongside AMD to also support [https://rocm.blogs.amd.com/ecosystems-and-partners/fortran-journey/README.html AMDs next-gen Fortran compiler], to offer an open-source alternative to CCE, but this effort is still in the very early stages.</ref>

<u>''Libraries''</u>
* Numerical libraries: FFTW, BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK. These are all provided via [https://www.amd.com/en/products/software/rocm/hpc.html AMDs ROCm] software stack, which includes hipFFT, hipBLAS, hipSolver, and more. We have tested ROCm versions 6.1, 6.3, and 6.4.
{{NB|important|We have seen dramatically improved performance in LAPACK and BLAS calls for ROCm versions 6.3 and 6.4 compared to earlier versions. For good performance, the latest ROCm install available in the CCE is highly recommended.|:}}
* A HIP-aware version of MPI. On CCE, this will be [https://www.mpich.org/ MPICH] (>=4).
* [https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/rccl/en/latest/ The ROCm Communication Collectives Library (RCCL)]. This library is not a strict requirement, but its use is highly recommended for performance reasons. Suitable installations of RCCL are shipped as part of ROCm.

<u>''Drivers''</u>
* GPU drivers for AMD datacenter GPUs are baked into the OS on HPC machines. The HIP-runtime and other parts of the user-space compute layer are shipped with ROCm. If you need to install your own drivers please follow the official [https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/install-on-linux/en/latest/install/quick-start.html# guide from AMD].

==== Intel GPUs ====

<u>''Compiler''</u>
* To compile the OpenMP offload version of VASP for AMD GPUS, the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/fortran-compiler.html Intel Fortran Compiler IFX] (>=2025.3.0) is needed. It is distributed via the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/hpc-toolkit.html oneAPI HPC Toolkit].
{{NB|warning|Older versions of the compiler might compile the code, but will lead to slow execution and/or wrong results at runtime. Thus, version 2025.3.0 or higher is a strict requirement!|:}}

<u>''Libraries''</u>
* Numerical libraries: FFTW, BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK. These are provided via the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/onemkl.html Intel Math Kernel Library (oneMKL)], which is distributed in the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/base-toolkit.html oneAPI Base Toolkit], and the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/hpc-toolkit.html oneAPI HPC Toolkit].
* A GPU-enabled version of MPI. We have both tested [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/mpi-library.html Intel-MPI], as distributed via the [https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/tools/oneapi/hpc-toolkit.html oneAPI HPC Toolkit] and [https://www.mpich.org/ MPICH] successfully.

<u>''Drivers''</u>
* GPU drivers for Intel datacenter GPUs are baked into the OS on HPC machines. We recommend using whatever your HPC center provides. If this is not possible or you want to install you own drivers, please follow the official [https://dgpu-docs.osgc.infra-host.com/driver/installation-lts2.html#installing-gpu-drivers Intel guide] and make sure that your OS is supported.

=== Hardware ===

==== NVIDIA GPUs ====

We have only tested the OpenACC GPU-port of VASP with the following NVIDIA GPUs:

* NVIDIA datacenter GPUs: P100 (Pascal), V100 (Volta), A30 & A100 (Ampere), and H100 (Hopper).
* NVIDIA Quadro GPUs: GP100 (Pascal), and GV100 (Volta). 
{{NB|important|Running VASP on other NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., "gaming" hardware) is technically possible but not advisable: these GPUs are not well suited since they do not offer fast double-precision floating-point arithmetic (FP64) performance and in general have smaller memories without error correction code (ECC) capabilities.|:}}

==== AMD GPUs ====

We have only tested the OpenMP offloading GPU-port of VASP with the following AMD datacenter GPUs:

* AMD Instinct MI210 & MI250x (CDNA 2), and  MI300A (CDNA 3).
{{NB|important|Running VASP on other AMD GPUs (e.g., Radeon PRO workstation cards, or "gaming" hardware) has not been tested at all to date|:}}

==== Intel GPUs ====

We have only tested the OpenMP offloading GPU-port of VASP with the following Intel datacenter GPUs:

* Intel Max 1100 and Intel Max 1150 (Ponte Veccio).
{{NB|important|Running VASP on other Intel GPUs (e.g., Intel Flex datacenter GPUs, Arc PRO workstation cards, or Arc "gaming" hardware) has not been tested at all to date|:}}

== Building ==

To build any GPU port of VASP it is best to base your <code>makefile.include</code> file on one of the [[makefile.include|archetypical templates]] and adapt these to the particulars of your system.
* For NVIDIA GPUs start from either <code>makefile.include.nvhpc_acc</code>, <code>makefile.include.nvhpc_omp_acc</code>, or <code>makefile.include.nvhpc_ompi_mkl_omp_acc</code>.
* For AMD GPUs start from <code>makefile.include.cray_omp_off</code>.
* For Intel GPUs start from <code>makefile.include.oneapi_omp_off</code>.

== Features and limitations ==

* Most features of VASP have been ported to GPU using OpenACC (NVIDIA), with the notable exception of everything involving the RPA: GW and ACFDT. This is work in progress. For the OpenMP offloading port (AMD & Intel), a few more features, e.g., [[:Category:Linear_response|linear response]] and [[Bethe-Salpeter-equations_calculations|BSE]], are still missing.
{{NB|mind|Unported features can still be used in the GPU build. They will just not run on the GPU, but on the host CPU.|:}}

* The use of parallel FFTs of the wave functions ({{TAG|NCORE}}>1) should be avoided for performance reasons. Currently, all GPU versions will automatically switch to {{TAG|NCORE}}=1 even if otherwise specified in the {{FILE|INCAR}} file.

* '''The GPU versions of VASP may only be executed using a single MPI-rank per available GPU:'''
: Using NCCL/RCCL has large performance benefits in the majority of cases, but it limits the number of ranks to one per device.
{{NB|mind|Some GPUs (e.g., AMD Mi250, Intel Max 1150) have 2 tiles or GCDs per physical device. Both those tiles will count as a separate GPU for this purpose, and VASP will allow, e.g., 8 ranks to run on 4 Mi250 GPUs, with a total of 8 GCDs.|:}}

== Running the GPU versions ==

<ol>
<li>
Use a single MPI rank per GPU.
</li>
<li>
Use OpenMP threads in addition to MPI ranks to leverage more of the available CPU power. The GPU versions are currently limited to the use of 1 MPI-rank/GPU, which means that potentially quite a bit of CPU power remains unused. Since there are still parts of the code that run CPU-side it can be beneficial to allow for the use of multiple OpenMP threads per MPI rank:
* The OpenMP offloading GPU port requires compilation with OpenMP and can use OpenMP on the CPU in those sections of the code that are not ported to GPU.
* To see how to build VASP with OpenACC- ''and'' OpenMP-CPU-support have a look at the [[Makefile.include.nvhpc ompi mkl omp acc|makefile.include.nvhpc_ompi_mkl_omp_acc]] file.
{{NB|important|Here we link against Intel's MKL library for CPU-sided FFTW, BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK calls and the Intel OpenMP runtime library (<tt>libiomp5.so</tt>). This is strongly recommended when compiling for Intel CPUs, especially when using multiple threads. To ensure that MKL uses the Intel OpenMP runtime library you need to set an environment variable, either by:
:<pre>export MKL_THREADING_LAYER=INTEL</pre>
:or by adding:
:<pre>-x MKL_THREADING_LAYER=INTEL</pre>
:as an option to your <code>mpirun</code> command.}}
* Correct [[Combining MPI and OpenMP|placement and pinning of OpenMPI ranks and OpenMP threads onto the CPU cores]] can be a bit tricky, and depends on the particular flavor of MPI one uses.
</li>
<li>
To achieve the best performance, it is important to choose {{TAG|KPAR}} and {{TAG|NSIM}} wisely. Unfortunately, the ideal values will depend on the particulars of your system, both in the sense of workload as well as hardware, so you will have to experiment with different settings. However, as a rule of thumb, one can say:
* Set {{TAG|KPAR}} to the number of GPUs (= MPI-ranks) you are going to use. This only makes sense, though, when the number of irreducible '''k'''-points in your calculation is more or less evenly divisible by {{TAG|KPAR}}, otherwise the distribution of the work over the MPI-ranks will be strongly imbalanced. This means your options in choosing this parameter are somewhat limited. 
* {{TAG|NSIM}} determines the number of bands that are optimized simultaneously in many of the electronic solvers (e.g RMM-DIIS and blocked-Davidson). As a rule, one should choose this parameter larger to get good performance on GPUs than one would for CPU-based execution.
{{NB|warning|For optimal CPU-based execution of VASP, one would normally experiment with different settings for {{TAG|NCORE}} as well. When running on GPUs, anything different from {{TAG|NCORE}}{{=}}1 will adversely affect performance, and VASP will automatically switch to {{TAG|NCORE}}{{=}}1, even if otherwise specified in the {{FILE|INCAR}} file.}}
</li>
</ol>

=== Environment variables ===

==== MPI ====
In contrast to OpenMPI, MPICH and Intel MPI have environment variables that can toggle GPU-aware MPI execution. Use the following settings:

* MPICH: <code>MPICH_GPU_SUPPORT_ENABLED=1</code>
* Intel MPI: <code>I_MPI_OFFLOAD=1</code> must be set to ensure that the GPUs can communicate directly.

==== OpenMP Offloading ====

* For GPU offloading, the OMP_STACKSIZE needs to be large. Set: <code>OMP_STACKSIZE=2048m</code>
* Both MKL and ROCm can leverage CPU threads in library calls that run on the GPU. Make sure you have enough threads (4-8) available.

===== AMD =====
* The cray compilers uses normal OpenMP threads that are set via: <code>OMP_NUM_THREADS=8</code>
* By default threads spin at 100% load in the cray omp runtime. You can safely disable this to give more headroom to ROCm helper threads by setting <code>export OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE</code>
* Currently VASP 6.6.0 cannot use shared memory as available on MI300A cards. Make sure that the feature is disabled at runtime via <code>export HSA_XNACK=0</code>
* To run on multiple AMD GPUs each MPI rank should only see its own GPU via <code>ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES</code> (will be fixed in future releases). To do so write a small wrapper script that is put in front of the VASP executable in your SLURM / PBS command: 
{{CB|#!/bin/bash
myGPU{{=}}${SLURM_LOCALID}
# for PBS use this:
#myGPU{{=}}${PMI_RANK}                                                                                 
export ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES{{=}}${myGPU}
exec $*|
:}}

===== Intel =====
* For Intel MKL, <code>MKL_NUM_THREADS</code> might be set. If it is too small, it can hurt performance, The savest way is to <code>unset MKL_NUM_THREADS</code> so that it defaults to <code>OMP_NUM_THREADS</code>, and set that.
